gui.serialcraft.io.direction.rx: Receives values from your device and converts them into redstone signals.
gui.serialcraft.io.signal.digital: Digital: off or on. Redstone 0 or 15; protocol 0 or 255.
gui.serialcraft.io.logic.or: OR takes the highest input level.

gui.serialcraft.io.help.channel.title: Communication channel
gui.serialcraft.io.help.channel.body:
A channel matches a module to a name in your firmware. If the sketch reads led_verde, enter led_verde here. A sensor can send pot_val:128.

Use 1–32 ASCII letters, digits, underscores (_), dots (.) or hyphens (-). Names are case-sensitive. The mc_ prefix is reserved for game telemetry.

Give independent actuators different channels; several receivers may share one channel.
gui.serialcraft.io.help.direction.title: Which way does the data travel?
gui.serialcraft.io.help.direction.body:
Minecraft → Hardware reads redstone and sends a value to your device. Example: a Minecraft lever controls a real LED.

Hardware → Minecraft receives a device value and emits redstone. Example: a real potentiometer changes a lamp’s redstone level.

Data direction is separate from connector roles. Green input faces receive redstone; red output faces emit it. One module uses one direction at a time.

Configure terminals on the block: right-click toggles input/off; Shift + right-click toggles output/off. There are north, south, east, west and bottom terminals. Bottom is selected from the module surface; there is no top terminal. Red outputs stay inactive in Minecraft → Hardware.
gui.serialcraft.io.help.signal.title: Digital and analog signals
gui.serialcraft.io.help.signal.body:
Digital means off or on: 0 or 15 redstone, 0 or 255 on the wire. Any positive value is on.

Analog keeps intermediate levels: 0–15 redstone and 0–255 on the wire. Redstone is multiplied by 17; received hardware values are divided by 17 and rounded. For example, 128 becomes redstone 8.

A microcontroller may use PWM to drive an output. PWM switches rapidly; it is not necessarily a continuous analog voltage.
gui.serialcraft.io.help.logic.title: How OR, AND and XOR work
gui.serialcraft.io.help.logic.body:
OR: highest input level.
AND: lowest input level, including zeros.
XOR: highest level only if an odd number of inputs are positive; otherwise zero.

These are level-combining rules, not bitwise operations on analog numbers.

Minecraft → Hardware combines green inputs into the transmitted value. Hardware → Minecraft uses a positive combined result to enable the received value, without changing its magnitude. With no inputs, reception passes directly and transmission sends zero.
gui.serialcraft.io.help.diagnostics.body:
RX is the last sample received from hardware. TX is the last value forwarded by the server to the client. TX is not an acknowledgement that the microcontroller received, confirmed or physically executed the command.

Read combines the green inputs. Processed is the result after logic and signal conversion. Output is the redstone actually emitted by this module.

Connection is the client’s report, not proof of actuator activity. RX age counts session ticks since reception. Silence alone does not establish a disconnection.

A stored -1 means no sample for RX, or no send for TX. The screen displays words instead of -1.
gui.serialcraft.io.discard.title: Discard unsaved changes?
gui.serialcraft.io.discard.body: Your edits have not been saved. Keep editing, or discard them and leave the editor.
gui.serialcraft.io.discard.pending: The server is validating your request. Leaving closes the editor but does not cancel a request already sent. Stay to see the result, or leave without confirmation.

gui.serialcraft.home.help.identity.title: Automatic board identification
gui.serialcraft.home.help.identity.body:
SerialCraft combines USB descriptors, startup banners and the identity reported by the firmware. The most reliable available source wins.

The badge distinguishes an unknown device, a USB bridge, a vendor, a detected model and a firmware declaration. Identification describes the device; it does not prove authentication. Connection details always come from the active transport.
gui.serialcraft.home.help.model.title: What does unconfirmed mean?
gui.serialcraft.home.help.model.body:
CH340, CH9102, CP210X and FTDI identify a USB-serial bridge, not an exact board. The same chip can appear on different Arduino or ESP boards.

SerialCraft only shows a model when the identification reaches model-level or firmware-declared confidence. Until then, the model remains unconfirmed. A firmware declaration is information supplied by the device.
gui.serialcraft.home.help.baud.title: Serial speed and firmware
gui.serialcraft.home.help.baud.body:
The baud rate must match Serial.begin(...) or its equivalent in your firmware. Select a value and use Apply and reconnect. The applied speed changes only after the port reopens successfully; errors remain visible.

Reopening can reset the board. Stop the waveform generator and let pending writes finish first. A successful port configuration does not confirm that the firmware uses the same speed. This setting does not control computer performance.
gui.serialcraft.home.help.wifi.title: Wi-Fi pairing and trust
gui.serialcraft.home.help.wifi.body:
The token pairs a temporary session. It stays hidden until you choose Show token. Use a trusted local network.

Remember board is available only when the existing authentication mechanism permits it and the board has announced a unique identity. Remembered boards use the existing challenge authentication on later connections. Forget board removes the saved trust and closes the current connection. The server can keep listening after a board disconnects.
